label: miso 64 classdonor
definition: miso-64 candidate (main) -- miso-63 keeper replay (miso-62 meta.json + miso_rpe_pricing + unit_outage_short_windows) + class_aware_fuel_price_fallback: the F923 nearby-donor pools consult same-class reporting plants first (measured basis: MISO 2024 CT filers $4.13/MMBtu cap-wtd vs CC $2.57; the class-blind quantity-weighted pool handed non-filing CTs the CC-dominated ~$2.6 price). Zero fitted parameters; docs/DIAGNOSIS-miso-july2025-lmp-2026-07.md §6 lane 1(b).
market_story: One real-market layer on the miso-63 keeper, zero fitted parameters: class-aware F923 fuel-cost gap-fill. Delivered gas is measurably class-priced — MISO 2024 CT filers pay $4.13/MMBtu capacity-weighted vs CC filers $2.57 (a +$1.56 small-volume/retail-transport premium) — but the 'nearby plant' donor pool the model used for the ~33% of CT capacity with no filing of its own was quantity-weighted and hence CC-burn-dominated (~$2.6), pricing those CTs ~$16-20/MWh below their measured class cost. With same-class donor pools (state, then zone, then the old class-blind fallback), 12 GW of gap-filled CT_PEAKER reprices $3.62 -> $4.48/MMBtu while CT_CHP (genuinely cheaper industrial contracts) drops $2.78 -> $2.52 — class fidelity cuts both ways. Result: the 2024 CT_PEAKER economic over-run at PRB's expense shrinks +7.1 -> +5.1 TWh, COAL_PRB narrows in both fail years (2023 -8.89 -> -8.47, 2024 -13.32 -> -12.41 TWh), 2025 total coal-over trims +9.9 -> +8.8 TWh (classFull basis), and every scored price metric moves toward actual (C3a-2025 -15.9% -> -15.4%, C3b-2025 0.206 -> 0.202, Indiana July-2025 +0.19); the two ungated 2025 C2 grid-basis diagnostics move slightly against (gas -6.1 -> -6.5%, coal-over +3.1 -> +3.4%). Fail set identical to the miso-63 keeper; C1 holds at the MISO-best 14/16 all / 10/12 free.
